content.title: About
content.content: Malted milk is a dairy beverage to which malted barley extract has been added. It has a mildly sweet, caramel‑like flavor and a creamy texture. The product is widely used in cooking, for desserts, shakes, and as a base for infant nutrition.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The malt extract gives the milk a characteristic golden hue.
Malted milk is a traditional ingredient in many Scandinavian recipes.
The lactose content may be slightly higher than in regular milk because of the added maltose.
It is often served chilled in summer and warm in winter.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Like regular milk, malted milk provides calcium essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Maltose contributes riboflavin (B2) and niacin (B3), which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Supports immunity
items.content: Vitamin D and vitamin A present in the milk help maintain immune function.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: The combination of lactose and maltose offers both quick and sustained energy.

items.title: Contains protein
items.content: Milk proteins (casein and whey) aid in tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance should limit intake or choose lactose‑free alternatives.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Allergy to casein or whey can cause reactions up to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Added maltose raises the total sugar level, which may be undesirable for diabetics.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Malted milk is more calorie‑dense than regular milk, so portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Malted milk can be enjoyed cold, blended into smoothies, added to porridge, baked goods, sauces, and desserts. It is often mixed into infant cereals to improve taste and energy content.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store malted milk in the refrigerator at 1‑4 °C. Once opened, consume within 5‑7 days. Do not freeze, as the texture may change.
